input_signals.name: Gross Profit Net Payout Bottleneck
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when strong industry-relative operating profitability coincides with net equity capital return through repurchases and dividends.
input_signals.reasoning: The bottleneck form scores firms highly only when both profitability and net payout are strong, avoiding the signed-product problem where weak-profit issuers could look attractive. Excluding gross debt issuance and repayment also reduces overlap with the broad net external financing anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( prstkc, dvc ), sstk ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post Interest Net Deleverager
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, xint), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong post-interest operating surplus that are actually reducing net debt intensity should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg measures a change in debt-to-assets rather than gross debt repayment, avoiding refinancing-churn contamination. Pairing deleveraging with post-interest operating profitability emphasizes balance-sheet repair funded by operating strength rather than simple liability turnover.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( ebitda, xint ), at ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Capped Net Buyback
input_signals.expression: SUB(MIN(RATIO(prstkc, at), RATIO(oancf, at)), RATIO(sstk, at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases should be most favorable when they are supported by operating cash generation and not offset by concurrent equity issuance.
input_signals.reasoning: The repurchase credit is capped by operating cash flow, so aggressive buybacks without cash support do not receive an inflated score. This avoids relying on share-count growth and instead tests whether buybacks are economically funded by current cash profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( min( ratio( prstkc, at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ), ratio( sstk, at ) )

input_signals.name: Dilution Resistant Profit Trend
input_signals.expression: SUB(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, csho), 5), TREND(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating profit per share improves faster than operating profit per asset should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This reframes share financing through the shareholder claim on operating profitability, rather than using raw share-count growth as a stand-alone anomaly. Comparing per-share and asset-scaled profit trends isolates whether financing behavior is making operating improvement accretive to each share.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( trend( ratio( oibdp, csho ), 5 ), trend( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Profit Net Debt Retirer
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong operating cash profitability that are net retiring long-term debt should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Using dltr minus dltis focuses on net long-term debt retirement rather than gross repayment churn or current-debt distress. The interaction tests whether cash profitability is strong enough to reduce creditor financing, rather than simply rewarding low leverage or high cash flow in isolation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Internally Financed R&D Cash Engine
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong pre-R&D operating cash generation, meaningful R&D intensity, and low external capital issuance should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding back R&D avoids double-penalizing an expense already reflected in operating cash flow, while treating unreported R&D as zero is economically natural. The signal targets firms able to fund intangible investment internally rather than firms whose R&D program depends on new equity or debt issuance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), min( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitable Cash Maturity Spread
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with strong reported operating profitability, those with better cash conversion and less current-debt pressure should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior short-term-debt stress signals produced stronger portfolio evidence than cross-sectional evidence, so this formulation creates a bipolar spread rather than a sparse short-only bottleneck. High values represent profitable firms whose earnings convert to cash without near-term refinancing strain, while low values identify profitable-looking firms exposed to cash and maturity pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), sub( rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), rank( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Cash Payoff Net Dilution
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms whose pre-R&D cash generation is improving without shareholder dilution should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts from static self-funding to realized R&D payoff net of dilution, so it is not the same three-way internal-financing screen. Non-R&D firms are not assigned a mechanical zero middle bucket; the R&D-intensity rank instead makes the strongest positive and negative signals come from firms where the intangible-investment mechanism is economically relevant.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Low Cost Liability Profit Quality
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(xint, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong industry-relative operating profitability and a low interest cost burden relative to liabilities should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The profitability leg no longer subtracts interest, so interest burden is not double-counted. Scaling interest expense by total liabilities gives a cleaner financing-cost measure than adding debt to assets, and the bottleneck rewards firms where operating strength is not being eroded by costly financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( xint, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self Funded Sales Margin Growth
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms growing sales while improving margins without heavy external financing should outperform externally financed growth with weak margin quality.
input_signals.reasoning: Sales growth is valuable when it scales profitably, but less so when funded through new capital while margins fail to expand. The signed spread makes the short side economically interpretable as growth financed by issuance rather than by operating improvement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( sale, 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Cash Maturity Shield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with strong pre-R&D cash generation and low current-debt pressure should outperform R&D firms whose intangible investment is exposed to maturity stress.
input_signals.reasoning: This combines the internally financed intangible channel with debt maturity risk rather than simply repeating an external-issuance screen. The signed spread keeps non-R&D firms closer to neutral while emphasizing R&D-heavy firms where cash generation and financing maturity are most economically relevant.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), sub( rank( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Backed Equity Issuer Quality
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, oancf), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance by cash-profitable, low-accrual firms should outperform equity issuance by firms whose reported operating profits are not cash-backed.
input_signals.reasoning: This revision abandons the blanket peak-profit issuer short story, which prior portfolio evidence contradicted, and instead diagnoses that some profitable issuers may be high-quality firms with valuable financing flexibility. Non-issuers are pushed toward neutral, while the long and short tails are separated among issuers by whether operating strength is cash-backed or accrual-heavy.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sstk, at ), 1 ), sub( rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( oiadp, oancf ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Current Debt R&D Retrenchment
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dlc, lt)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D firms with high current-debt pressure that are cutting R&D intensity without strong pre-R&D cash generation should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids recombining the prior R&D cash-maturity and growth-maturity winners, and instead tests whether short-term financing pressure forces intangible underinvestment. The high-signal short leg is not simply R&D-heavy growth; it is a maturity-pressure case where apparent cash constraints coincide with R&D retrenchment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dlc, lt ) ), sub( rank( neg( delta( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 1 ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dilutive Buyback Cash Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(prstkc, at), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms reporting large repurchases while share count still rises and operating cash profitability is weak should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the debt-issuer margin spread and focuses on buyback effectiveness: gross repurchase dollars are suspect when they fail to reduce dilution. Pairing the dilution outcome with operating cash profitability distinguishes cash-backed shareholder return from repurchases that merely offset equity compensation or financing needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( prstkc, at ), 1 ), sub( rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Levered Cash Carry Advantage
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Liability-intensive firms should outperform when operating cash generation per dollar of liabilities exceeds the interest cost burden.
input_signals.reasoning: The liability-intensity gate makes the signal about productive use of financing rather than a trivial profitability-minus-interest spread across all firms. High values identify firms where liabilities appear to fund cash-generating operations at a favorable carry, while low values capture leveraged firms whose cash output does not cover financing cost well.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( lt, at ) ), sub( rank( ratio( oancf, lt ) ), rank( ratio( xint, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Lagged Capital Profit Payoff
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital in the prior period should outperform when operating profitability improves faster than the asset base expands.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the weak lagged-capital-raise short idea by asking whether financing produced operating payoff, not merely whether profitability declined. High values identify prior capital raisers with improving profit productivity, while low values capture asset expansion without corresponding operating gains.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( lag( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), 1 ), 1 ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), rank( growth( at, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Costly Debt Paydown Cash Relief
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(RATIO(xint, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-generative firms retiring high-cost debt should outperform firms continuing to issue or roll into costly debt.
input_signals.reasoning: Net long-term debt retirement alone had strong cross-sectional evidence but weak alpha, so this conditions paydown on the economic benefit of retiring expensive liabilities. The signal is highest when cash flow can fund relief from high interest burden and lowest when costly debt exposure is being increased.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ), 1 ), min( rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), rank( ratio( xint, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Externally Funded R&D Commercialization Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), SUB(RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(revt, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms raising external capital while R&D intensity rises faster than revenue productivity should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the current-debt/R&D-retrenchment setup with a commercialization-failure mechanism: external capital is funding intangible buildout, but sales productivity is not following. The short leg is not simply maturity pressure or weak cash flow; it is financed R&D expansion without evidence of revenue conversion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), 1 ), sub( rank( trend( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 5 ) ), rank( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity Deleveraging Cash Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(sstk, at), 1), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuers should outperform when proceeds appear to support debt reduction and the firm is not issuing to cover weak operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This treats equity issuance as potentially constructive when it repairs the balance sheet rather than as uniformly negative dilution. The low tail is economically interpretable as equity issuers with poor cash generation and net debt expansion, while the high tail captures cash-generative deleveraging issuers.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sstk, at ), 1 ), sub( rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: External Capital Operating Leverage Payoff
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(oibdp, 1)), RANK(GROWTH(xsga, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that recently raised external capital should outperform when operating profit grows faster than overhead.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether external financing translates into operating leverage rather than organizational bloat. High values indicate prior capital raises followed by profit scaling faster than SG&A, while low values identify externally funded overhead growth without commensurate operating payoff.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( lag( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), 1 ), 1 ), sub( rank( growth( oibdp, 1 ) ), rank( growth( xsga, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Payoff Shareholder Accretion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, csho), 5)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms should outperform when intangible investment translates into rising operating profit per share without dilution.
input_signals.reasoning: This leaves the cash-maturity channel and instead tests whether R&D spending is becoming accretive to existing shareholders. The financing leg is share dilution, but it is evaluated only in the context of per-share operating-profit payoff from intangible investment rather than as a standalone net-share-issuance anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), sub( rank( trend( ratio( oibdp, csho ), 5 ) ), rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Lagged Capital Gross Profit Payoff
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at), 1), 1), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that raised external capital should outperform when subsequent gross-profit productivity improves faster than the asset base expands.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the growth indicator with a lagged financing-payoff test, avoiding the middle-bucket problem for non-growers. The signal asks whether external capital translated into better gross operating economics rather than mere balance-sheet expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( lag( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ), 1 ), 1 ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( growth( at, 1 ) ) ) )
